issues.desc: Scope anchored to a "Milestone 2-6" roadmap with no persisted canonical source: grep across the repo finds the six-milestone roadmap only as an oblique reference in B-42c0 background ("建议中的六个 milestone", a prior user suggestion), not in any docs/requirements/decisions doc. "Milestone N" is also overloaded (B-95d8 reuses it for unrelated story-internal phases). Each CHK context paraphrases its own milestone inline (mitigates actionability), but PLAN/scope-plan review cannot independently verify coverage (do the 5 items faithfully cover Milestones 2-6, what did Milestone 1 deliver). Recommend PLAN pin the six-milestone roadmap + Milestone-1 status into background.md or a decision doc.

Large, high-risk scope in one story: 5 milestone-sized items (evidence quality scoring gate, reviewer quorum/differentiated verifier, structured CI/human attestation, actor trust registry+revocation, external fact provenance/freshness), each adding new gate/policy/CLI surface on top of the gate+validate machinery flagged in riskSignals. This is the multi-gate/policy surface CLAUDE.md 合并态组合审查 warns about. Not a blocker (user explicitly requested Milestones 2-6 together; per-item dispatch supported), but PLAN must produce per-item decision + >=3 preMortem and apply combination-review discipline; consider whether some items warrant separate stories.

userSees describe behavior, not precise output text. CLAUDE.md requires userSees to contain exact observable output strings, not abstract descriptions; current values ("blocks weak evidence", "reports reviewer quorum status", "fails clearly when stale or empty") are behavioral. PLAN should refine each into the concrete CLI/diagnostic text validate/gate emits so verificationIntent is mechanically checkable.

userSees fields are capability-level assertions ("can reject", "blocks", "flags") rather than a watchable forge-attempt->rejection. For a forgery-defense feature, demonstrability IS the user value. Recommend PLAN define at least one concrete transcript per milestone: actor attempts to fake X -> Koala emits message Y and blocks, so the operator can verifiably say done rather than trusting that the gate exists.
